cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul wants them informed so they won't grieve like those without hope. He says, “…so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.” Notice he never says don't grieve at all. He says don't grieve like people who have no hope. I think he knows it hurts, and he's handing them something solid to hold while it does.

The answer is that God will bring them with Jesus. Paul says “…God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him.” Look at how he builds it. Jesus died and rose again, so those who are in Him are not left behind. If Jesus got back up, they come along with Him.

The answer is False. Paul says those who are alive and remain “…will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.” The believers who have died are not at the back of the line, friends. Nobody is cutting in front of them.

The answer is the trumpet of God. Paul says the Lord will come “…with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God…” That's three sounds in one verse, friends. I've heard a lot of timers go off in my bakery, and not a single one is in this league.

The answer is dead. Paul says “…the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.” Those who died believing in Jesus go first, friends. Paul follows it up with “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” (1 Thessalonians 4:18), so this is meant to lift people up.

The answer is True. Paul says the living “…will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air.” The word that stands out to me is together, friends. Nobody makes the trip alone.
The answer is always! Paul says, “And so we will always be with the Lord.” Then he adds, “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” (1 Thessalonians 4:18) It's not a quick visit, friends.
The answer is True. Paul says, “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” The words are for lifting each other up, friends. They're meant to be shared, not kept in a drawer.

The answer is like a thief in the night. Paul says, “…the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.” A thief doesn't send a schedule, friends. That's the picture Paul wants stuck in their minds.

The answer is destruction. Paul says “destruction will come upon them suddenly…” and he says it comes while people are saying, “Peace and security…” That word suddenly matters, friends. It lands right in the middle of everybody saying things are fine.
The answer is False. Paul says destruction will come upon them suddenly, “…like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.” There's no back door, friends. They will not escape.

The answer is that they are not in the darkness. Paul says, “But you, brothers, are not in the darkness so that this day should overtake you like a thief.” A thief works in the dark, and these believers aren't in it. That's why the day won't catch them off guard the way it does others.

The answer is True. Paul says, “So then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us remain awake and sober.” Since they belong to the day, they live like it, friends. He even includes himself with the words let us.

The answer is faith and love. Paul says, “…putting on the breastplate of faith and love…” A breastplate guards the chest, and he makes it out of faith and love. Not a bad thing to wear to work, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, “For God has not appointed us to suffer wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.” What they were appointed for is salvation, through Jesus. That's good news worth repeating, friends.

The answer is live together. Paul says Jesus “…died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.” Awake or asleep, friends, the answer is the same. It's together with Him.

The answer is build one another up. Paul says, “Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.” Notice the last part, friends. He's not scolding them, because they're already doing it.
